title: Bix after Whiteman and studio reading skills
summary: Challis doubts the story that Whiteman offered Bix a job later, explaining Bix could read but lacked studio expertise.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: What about Bix and Trumbauer? Had they gone already, or were they still there.
No, I think -- Trumbauer I think was still there.
Yeah, and they never got him back in the band, which is another item that's questionable with all this. There are some guys, particularly the book says that Paul offered him a job.

Yeah. Said that Whiteman offered him a job. Well, I'm positive that Whiteman didn't. I wouldn't go out on a limb and say that, but actually I can't say it because I wasn't there, but they didn't get him in there. Bix was the kind of a guy that could, as I say, if Charlie were there and he had good guys surrounding him that could read, he could read. No problem.

But to take a part and mark it, segue down to here, cut here and move down to here, that's studio expertise and Charlie had that and a lot of the other guys in the band had that, but not Bix. Bix wants to know on his part, where do I

come in? What do I do to play? And you write a few things out for him, he'll play anything, as far as that's concerned, but to do that studio stuff, it was not for Bix. I would say. They always say that he wasn't really happy in that situation.
